**Yes, but only some portable power stations can.** A basic one can keep a computer running in an outage, but it may still cut power for a moment during the switchover and reboot a desktop ([Anker](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups)).

**What to check**
- **Documented UPS or EPS mode** with automatic switchover. Pass-through charging alone isn't UPS protection ([Anker](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/home-power-backup/portable-power-station-ups-home-server-nas)).
- **Transfer time.** Anker says 10 or 20 ms is fast but not 0 ms, so check your computer's power supply manual. If it requires 0 ms, use an online double-conversion UPS instead.
- **Pure sine wave output**, which suits computers and other devices with switching power supplies.
- **Enough wattage and watt-hours.** Measure your PC's actual draw with a plug-in watt meter. Runtime is roughly Wh × 0.85 ÷ load in watts, so a 1,000 Wh unit running a 100 W load lasts about 8.5 hours at best.

EcoFlow warns that 20 to 30+ ms switchovers risk data loss ([EcoFlow](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply)). That is a seller's claim, and Anker is more measured, so your power supply's manual is the better guide. A laptop has its own battery and is much less sensitive.

**Models with published UPS specs**
- [Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups): 10 ms switchover, 2,010 Wh, 1,500 W pure sine wave. It was listed at $699.99 after coupon. This link goes to Anker's article, which has the shop link.
- [EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply): under 10 ms, 600 W. That's enough for a typical desktop and drives, but the article gave no price and its link goes to the article, not a store page.
- [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2): ≤15 ms switchover, 2,073.6 Wh, 2,600 W. It's $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF, which the listing says was tested in Bluetti's cart today. This is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you. At 15 ms it's the slowest of the three, so check your power supply's tolerance first.

I'd go with the S2000 or RIVER 3 Plus for a desktop. If your PC runs anything critical, such as a NAS, a server, or active database writes, an online UPS is the safer choice.

If you tell me your PC's wattage and how long you want it to run, I can narrow this down.
